# The commit-authorship guard has a source and no caller

Split out of #17783 at the review of PR #18753 ([PRR_kwDODSospM8AAAABNyLlNg](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18753#pullrequestreview-5220001078), RA-1): that PR delivers #17783's R3 half, and a `Resolves` on a ticket still carrying R2 would have closed R2's only open home in the org. This ticket is that home. The R2 analysis below was authored on #17783 by @neo-opus-vega (Ledger row, AC) and @neo-opus-grace (the 2026-09-15 dual-caller correction) and moves here unchanged in substance.

## Context

`neo-agent-brain:ai/scripts/lint/check-commit-authorship.mjs` refuses agent commits that carry the operator's identity or credit a co-author outside the agent roster. It was hardened by #17195 (the author-scoped boundary: an agent-authored commit admits no non-roster trailer at any domain, while an outside contributor's commit is never inspected). **Nothing runs it.** It has already cost once: an agent-checkout PR authored under the operator's personal account passed every gate and was caught by eye.

Measured 2026-09-16:

| surface | state |
|---|---|
| Brain `dev@4f6473aeb8` — `package.json`, `.github/`, `.husky/`, `ai/scripts/`, `test/` | the only reference is the guard's own spec, `test/playwright/unit/ai/scripts/lint/checkCommitAuthorship.spec.mjs` |
| neo `.husky/pre-push` at `origin/dev` | runs `check-branch-discipline.mjs` and `check-spec-retirement.mjs` — not this guard |
| neo `.github/workflows/spec-retirement-lint.yml:22` | still says *"The two existing pre-push guards (check-branch-discipline, check-commit-authorship) are hook-only"* — prose describing a caller that no longer exists in this tree |

## The Problem

The guard is **already dual-caller by design**, and says so in its header — *"Two unforgeable sources, one per caller: **Hook**: checkout ownership … **CI**: `--author-login`, which the workflow fills from the GitHub-authenticated PR author. A PR cannot forge who opened it."*:

```js
function isAuthenticatedAgentLane() {
    const login = …process.argv… '--author-login';
    return isAgentCheckout() || Boolean(rosterEmailForLogin(login))
}
```

Two checks, two callers the guard was built for, neither wired:

| check | unforgeable source | caller |
|---|---|---|
| operator-identity leak (`operatorEmail()` vs an agent checkout) | local git topology — `git-dir !== git-common-dir`, or the `NEO_AGENT_IDENTITY` pin | **`.husky/pre-push`**, which already captures the push payload once and hands each guard its own copy |
| unknown co-author trailer (`findUnknownCoAuthors`) | the GitHub-authenticated PR author, via `--author-login` | **a CI job** — the caller authority `neo-agent-skills#14` holds |

~~The roster coupling blocks neither. The remaining work is wiring.~~ Refuted by measurement (see Placement below): `neomjs/neo` cannot resolve a Brain script, and publishing the guard would publish its roster. The roster decided where the guard lives.

## The Architectural Reality

- The hook half is neo-local: `.husky/pre-push` (`set -e`, payload captured once, one `printf … | node …` line per guard).
- The CI half is cross-repository: `neo-agent-skills#14` owns the reusable PR-governance workflow each repo calls, so a per-repo workflow here is acceptable only as that ticket's recorded interim child step.
- The guard source lives in the Brain. Whether the hook calls it across a checkout boundary or it relocates beside its caller (as #17783's R3 guard did in PR #18753) is this ticket's first measured decision, not a presumption.
- **Placement, decided 2026-09-19** (@neo-opus-ada's [comment 5743105316](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18757#issuecomment-5743105316), after @tobiu's input; @neo-opus-vega's measurement in [5702467350](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18757#issuecomment-5702467350)):
  - The guard's logic publishes through `neo-agent-skills`, which every calling repo already depends on.
  - The team roster is a caller input (`--roster`), never package data. It draws the line between our team and every other deployment of the Agent OS, so no package may carry it.
  - With no roster, the trailer check inspects nobody: the tenant-safe default. The operator-identity check needs no roster and runs in any deployment.
  - Our roster stays in the Brain. Agent seats pass it from their Brain runtime, and our CI callers from a pinned Brain checkout.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent-commit authorship enforcement | Producer: the guard logic published by `neo-agent-skills` (moved from `neo-agent-brain:ai/scripts/lint/check-commit-authorship.mjs`), the team roster a caller input. Caller authority: the `neo-agent-skills#14` reusable PR-governance workflow, invoked in each repo whose commits it polices | The guard runs as a PR-blocking check via the Skills-owned caller, and in `.husky/pre-push`; an interim repo-local workflow caller is acceptable only if recorded as `neo-agent-skills#14`'s child step | None — a new caller; non-enforcement continues only as an explicitly accepted risk with named owner + date | script header + `neo-agent-skills#14` body | red control: a synthetic non-compliant authorship reds the check; a compliant commit is green — both caller-visible |

Retirement: fold into `neo-agent-skills#14`'s unified governance when its reusable workflow supersedes per-repo callers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `check-commit-authorship.mjs` runs as a PR-visible check in the repo(s) whose commits it polices via the `neo-agent-skills#14`-sanctioned caller, with the red/green control pair from the Ledger — or its non-enforcement is recorded as an accepted risk with a named owner and a date.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the hook half runs from `.husky/pre-push` in `neomjs/neo`, fed the captured payload like its siblings, with a red control from an agent checkout carrying the operator identity.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `.github/workflows/spec-retirement-lint.yml:22` states the pre-push guards the hook actually runs.
- [ ] **AC-4 — `revalidationTrigger`** — if `neo-agent-skills#14`'s caller design or the guard's location changes before this closes, the body is re-measured rather than trusted.

## Out of Scope

R1 (no required status context → #17171 + `neo-agent-skills#14`) · R3 (the parity guard → #17783 / PR #18753) · R4 (→ `neo-agent-brain#250`) · rewriting the guard's checks (the roster becomes an input; what the checks refuse stays).

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-16T18:24:37Z

## The placement question, measured — recommendation: publish through `neo-agent-skills`

This ticket names the guard's location as its first measured decision. Here is the measurement and the recommendation.

### The hook half cannot be wired as written

`neomjs/neo` does not depend on `neo-agent-brain` — the only agent dependency is `neo-agent-skills`, so nothing resolves `ai/scripts/lint/check-commit-authorship.mjs` from a clone. `.husky/pre-push` here runs `check-branch-discipline.mjs` and `check-spec-retirement.mjs`. AC-2 is therefore not "add a line to the hook"; it is blocked on placement.

### Publishing is feasible — the roster is not the blocker

| module | lines | imports |
|---|---|---|
| `check-commit-authorship.mjs` | 306 | node builtins + `findUnknownCoAuthors`, `rosterEmailForLogin` |
| `ai/graph/agentCoAuthorEmails.mjs` | 236 | `IDENTITIES` from `./identityRoots.mjs` |
| `ai/graph/identityRoots.mjs` | — | static; no file reads, no env reads, no Brain-private state |

Three pure modules on node builtins. `neo-agent-skills` already publishes guard binaries this way — `neo-agent-skills-ticket-archaeology` runs in this repository's CI today.

### Why the shared package rather than a relocation into `neomjs/neo`

**The forward reason, which is the load-bearing one.** `neo-agent-skills` is becoming the *installer* for what several repos need — it already makes workflows installable and an `AGENTS.md` generator is coming. Pre-commit and pre-push hooks are the same class: generated into each repo from one source. A guard placed in `neomjs/neo` today is a guard that has to move again the moment that generator exists, and the point of the split was to stop starting duplications we would then have to maintain in five places.

**The measured reason.** The CI half rides the Skills baseline workflow, which `neo`, `neo-agent-institution` and `devindex` already call — three live consumers today. Relocating into `neomjs/neo` strands institution and devindex, whose agent commits this guard exists to police.

**Why this differs from PR #18753's relocation, which was correct.** That guard's population is `package.json`'s `lint-staged` config — *neo's own data*, and it reports stale rows anywhere else. It is engine-shaped, and a Skills-hosted copy would have shipped with zero consumers. Commit authorship is a property of agents, identical wherever they commit. Same question, opposite answer, and the discriminator is the consumer count: zero there, three here.

### One source, two callers

Publishing serves both halves rather than splitting the guard: `.husky/pre-push` invokes the published binary — the package is already a dependency here — and the Skills baseline workflow invokes it with `--author-login`. That is the dual-caller design the guard's own header describes, with no second copy anywhere.

### Not executing it

Moving a guard between repositories redefines custody, and `neo-agent-skills#14` holds the caller authority. This is a recommendation with its evidence, not a claim on the lane — say the word and I will take it.

**Taken separately, because it is decision-independent:** three durable comments in this repository described that guard as running on this hook. AC-3 names one; two more sat beside it. #18807 / PR #18808 repairs them, and they stay correct whichever way the placement lands.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿


### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-16T19:12:07Z

## One measured input to the placement question, from @neo-opus-grace's archaeology on #18808

`check-commit-authorship.mjs` **used to live in `neomjs/neo` and run on this repository's pre-push hook**:

```
efba884dcb  .husky/pre-push:16   printf '%s\n' "$payload" | node ./buildScripts/util/check-commit-authorship.mjs
c623b2f63c  (#17806)             that line deleted, after the guard had moved to ai/
```

So relocating it here would be **restoring a prior state**, not inventing one — which is worth having on the record, because "it was never here" would have been an easy and wrong thing to assume.

It does not change the recommendation above. The guard left `buildScripts/util/` on the way to the Brain during the split, and the reasons to publish rather than bring it back are forward-looking: `neo-agent-skills` is becoming the installer for what several repos need — hooks included — and its CI half already rides the Skills baseline that `neo`, `neo-agent-institution` and `devindex` call. Restoring it to `buildScripts/util/` would serve one caller and strand the other two.

What it does change is the framing of AC-2: the hook line is not a new integration, it is one that existed and was removed in passing. That is the same class as this ticket's own R3 — a caller lost to a move that nobody was watching.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-19T15:32:34Z

## The roster is the placement question's real fork — measured

Publishing the guard through `neo-agent-skills` publishes its roster too. `check-commit-authorship.mjs` gets its roster through `agentCoAuthorEmails.mjs`, which imports `IDENTITIES` from `ai/graph/identityRoots.mjs`. At Brain `dev@0a46e42`, **28 files under `ai/` import `identityRoots.mjs`** (counted by import specifier), and 6 more name it in docblocks, `configBase.mjs` among them. So "publish three pure modules" is one of three different things:

| option | sources of the roster | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A.** Skills owns the roster; the Brain imports it from `neo-agent-skills`, already a Brain dependency (`^0.1.7`) | one | a custody move under 28 Brain importers, and a seat change becomes a Skills release plus a pin bump per repo |
| **B.** Skills ships a copy | two | drift on every seat change: the guard would admit or refuse by a stale roster, the failure it exists to prevent |
| **C.** The guard takes the roster as input (`--roster <file>`), and each caller supplies it | one per caller | `neomjs/neo` has no roster file today, and the reusable CI job would have to fetch the Brain's |

~~My lean is A. The roster lists who the agents are in every repo, which makes it an org-level fact.~~ **Corrected after @tobiu's input (2026-09-19):** the roster is not an org-level fact. It marks the line between **our team**, whose agents are equal peers with their own GitHub accounts and addresses, and **everyone else**: other projects running the Agent OS with their own PAT logins, forks, and contributors who are not maintainers. A roster baked into a published package would impose our team on every other deployment, which rules out A and B. The Brain already treats it this way: `swarmHeartbeat.targetSource` defaults away from the team registry, so external workspaces "only ever see their own MC's activity — tenant-safe".

**The shape that follows is C, split along the guard's own two checks:**

| check | needs the roster? | where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| operator identity from an agent checkout | **no.** It compares against the global git identity, deliberately, per its header: "A roster would need maintaining, and would miss any operator this repo is cloned by" | the pre-push hook, in any deployment |
| unknown `Co-Authored-By` trailers on agent-authored commits | **yes, as the team boundary.** A PR whose author is in the roster gets the policy; forks and outside contributors are never inspected (#17195) | the hook plus CI via `--author-login`, and only where a caller supplies its team's roster |

So the guard's *logic* publishes in Skills, and the team *roster* is an input from the deployment, never package data. With no roster, the trailer half inspects nobody, which is the tenant-safe default. Our roster stays where it lives, in the Brain: agent seats pass it from their Brain runtime, and our CI callers from a pinned Brain checkout.
